turns.t: Hi, thank you for seeing me. I hit my head two days ago, and I've had a headache since, and I wanted to make sure it's nothing serious.
Of course. Tell me exactly what happened. ~
I was on a ladder at work, about eight feet, slipped on the third rung and came down on my right side, my head hit the concrete. ~
Did you lose consciousness?
No, I don't think so. I was dazed for a minute, but I remember everything, including the ambulance guy asking my name.
Good. Tell me about the headache.
It's a dull ache, all across the back and the right side. Worse in the afternoon. It started the same evening.
Any nausea?
A bit queasy, mostly the first day. Still a little today.
Is the light bothering you? ~
A little, yes, I've kept the blinds down. ~
Is there anything you've been taking for it? ~
Not yet. I didn't want to mask anything. ~
Good thinking. Do you have any health conditions?
Migraines, since college. And high blood pressure, but it's controlled with exercise.
What do you do for work?
I'm a construction foreman. Mostly on sites, rarely on ladders, which is the irony.
Let me take your numbers. Blood pressure 128 over 80, pulse 68, and oxygen 98 percent.
Is that fine? ~
That's fine. Let me look at your head. Tell me when it's tender.
There. Ow. That's the spot. ~
There's a bruise and a tender swelling on the right side at the back of your head, about the size of an egg.
I haven't looked. ~
Now follow my finger with your eyes, without moving your head.
Like this? ~
Your pupils are equal and react to light, and your eye movements are normal.
That's good, right? ~
Very. Now walk the line to the door and back, heel to toe.
That's a bit wobbly. ~
It's steady enough. Your balance is normal.
Phew. ~
Any weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking since the fall?
No, nothing like that. My speech is normal, and my arms and legs feel fine.
Here's what I think. This looks like a concussion, but with a head injury like this, I can't rule out a small bleed inside the head.
A bleed? ~
It's unlikely, but I'd rather be safe. I'd like to arrange a CT scan of your head today.
Okay. How long does it take? ~
The scan takes minutes, the wait is longer. I'd also like to start paracetamol, 1 gram, every six hours, for the headache.
No ibuprofen? ~
Avoid ibuprofen for now. And rest, no work, no screens for a day or two.
Fair enough. ~
If the headache gets worse, you vomit, or you feel confused or very drowsy, come back to the emergency department immediately.
Understood. Thank you. ~
